items.title: OpenAPI document lists a 400 application/problem+json response for POST /api/orders/draft
covers: Expected: OpenAPI document lists a 400 response for POST /api/orders/draft with application/problem+json
items.reason: This is the defect itself: the served contract omitted the 400 that the draft endpoint returns for an item-less draft, so clients and generated SDKs did not know the validation error exists. It is a functional case because the document is generated at runtime from endpoint metadata (`.ProducesProblem(400)` on the mapping), which only a running app with the real OpenAPI pipeline produces; a unit test of the handler cannot see it.

items.title: The 400 the OpenAPI document declares references the problem details schema
covers: Expected: 400 response with a problem details body
items.reason: The story requires the documented 400 to carry "a problem details body", not just a media type; an SDK generator uses the schema to build the error type, so a 400 entry with no or the wrong schema would still leave clients unable to read the error. It is separate from TC-BUG-32-01 because a document can list the media type with an empty schema. Functional for the same reason as TC-BUG-32-01: the schema is produced by the runtime OpenAPI generator.

items.title: OpenAPI document still lists the 200 application/json OrderDraftDTO response for POST /api/orders/draft
covers: Expected: The endpoint's behaviour is unchanged (contract side)
Deviations: Ok<OrderDraftDTO> still supplies the 200 response
items.reason: Adding explicit response metadata (`.ProducesProblem`) to an endpoint can change how the generator merges the `Results<...>` union's metadata; if the 200 entry disappeared or lost its schema, the fix would trade one contract gap for a worse one. The story says the endpoint is otherwise unchanged, so its documented success response must still be there. Functional because only the running generator produces the document.

items.title: Draft with no items still returns 400 application/problem+json, matching the documented response
covers: Expected: The endpoint's behaviour is unchanged
items.reason: The story's Expected says the documented 400 must match what step 2 returns, and the endpoint's behaviour must not change; this case pins the runtime side of that match (status, media type, problem fields) so a change that edits the handler while fixing the contract is caught. Functional because the status code and content type come from the real HTTP pipeline.

items.title: Draft with one item still returns 200 with the order draft
covers: Expected: The endpoint's behaviour is unchanged
items.reason: The story requires the endpoint's behaviour to stay unchanged; the success path is the behaviour most clients depend on, and a fix that touches the endpoint mapping could break it (for example by altering how the body binds). Functional because it needs the real binding, MediatR handler and serialization.
